Michael Burry's latest move puts the Nasdaq 100 under scrutiny
Hillary Remy
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 3:07 PM CST 4 min read
NVDA
^NDX
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Michael Burry is not buying the bounce. "The Big Short" investor said he used the Nasdaq 100's rebound off the 27,000 level to double his put position on the index. He compared its Oct. 6 high to the March 2000 peak that came before the dot-com crash.

"Behold the bull-trap," he wrote on his personal Substack post.

He saved his bluntest message for Nvidia.

"NVIDIA bulls will have another fluffy big chance to get out. Get out," Burry wrote, warning that the company's "business will not disappear, but its growth may slow and, critically, its margins may fall."

Michael Burry has been moving toward this view for weeks. In September, he swapped several outright shorts for long-dated puts and said new research led him to "move timelines up" from his earlier 2028 base case.

"The bubble in AI may burst sooner than later," he wrote, adding, "Puts expire. Shorts do not." His positions then already included Nasdaq 100 puts in the 24,000s expiring in September 2027.

Why Burry sees a bull-trap in the Nasdaq

Michael Burry laid out the trade in a Nov. 12 post on his Substack, Cassandra Unchained. The new puts expire in early 2027 with a strike roughly 20% below the index level.

He placed the trade as the index rebounded, and he expects a significant correction in chip and tech stocks before mid-2027. Because he no longer files quarterly 13F reports, the size of the bet is unknown.

Also read: Michael Burry has a surprising new take on Nvidia stock

The market has already given ground. The Invesco QQQ Trust, which tracks the Nasdaq 100, closed on Nov. 13 at $679.89, down 10.5% from its Oct. 6 close. Short interest in the fund has climbed to 11% of shares outstanding, the highest since 2023, based on figures from The Kobeissi Letter, as reported by 24/7 Wall St.

Burry also widened his bet against chipmakers. He bought back the 25% of his VanEck Semiconductor ETF puts that he had trimmed on Nov. 5, positions that expire in June 2027, and he named Broadcom and AMD as likely winners if Nvidia's grip loosens.

Michael Burry tells Nvidia bulls to get out

Burry ties much of his Nvidia call to Jensen Huang's exit.

"The Don was the Enforcer. NVIDIA is losing both," he wrote. He warned that "the threat for NVIDIA and its AI ecosystem is that the cash may cease to flow," with customers able to renegotiate, slow deals or switch suppliers.

He also said he found leverage "upwards of 76x" in the system.  

He has also questioned how Nvidia props up demand.

"The Don has fallen," he wrote. The company bought $42.4 billion of equity securities in the first half of fiscal 2027, and in August it teamed up with firms including Apollo, BlackRock and Blackstone to mobilize more than $500 billion for AI infrastructure.

US stock index futures pointed to a mixed opening on Tuesday, with Nasdaq 100 futures rising 0.3% while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures declined 0.8%, following substantial losses across Wall Street in the previous session.

Technology shares showed signs of stabilisation after several sessions of declines, with investors awaiting quarterly results from Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and assessing the implications of additional US restrictions on access to advanced artificial intelligence chips.

Meanwhile, Home Depot (NYSE:HD) shares fell 2.4% in pre-market trading despite the retailer reporting quarterly earnings and revenue above analyst expectations.

The contrasting movements suggested that the Nasdaq could recover some of its recent losses, while weakness in individual Dow components could weigh on the blue-chip index.

Nvidia Shares Rise Ahead of Third-Quarter Earnings

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) shares advanced 0.8% in pre-market trading ahead of the company's fiscal third-quarter earnings announcement, scheduled for after Tuesday's market close.

The increase followed a 4.1% decline in the previous session, when concerns surrounding the company's leadership transition and future performance contributed to selling pressure.

Nvidia's upcoming results are being closely monitored because of the company's position in the artificial intelligence semiconductor market.

Daniela Hathorn, Senior Market Analyst at Capital.com, said the earnings announcement could influence investor sentiment across the technology sector.

"Strong results could help restore confidence in the AI sector, although even an earnings beat may not be enough if management fails to address concerns about future investment returns," Hathorn said.

"Conversely, disappointing guidance could accelerate the selloff."

Investors will be assessing Nvidia's quarterly financial performance alongside management's outlook for demand, capital investment and future earnings.

Home Depot Shares Decline Despite Earnings Beat

Home Depot (NYSE:HD) fell approximately 2.4% in pre-market trading, potentially adding downward pressure to the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

The home improvement retailer reported fiscal third-quarter results that exceeded analysts' expectations for both revenue and earnings.

However, the company's shares declined following the announcement, which also included changes to its senior management.

Home Depot said Chief Financial Officer Richard McPhail would succeed Ted Decker as Chief Executive Officer, with the appointment taking effect the following week.

US stock futures moved lower on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, as investors awaited quarterly results from Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and assessed developments surrounding the semiconductor company's leadership, new US restrictions on artificial intelligence chip exports and the outlook for interest rates.

At 08:50 GMT, Nasdaq 100 futures were down 31 points, or 0.1%, while S&P 500 futures declined 20 points, or 0.3%. Dow Jones futures fell 225 points, equivalent to 0.4%.

The declines followed losses on Wall Street during the previous session, when technology shares came under selling pressure amid uncertainty surrounding Nvidia and the broader artificial intelligence sector.

Nvidia Results to Test AI Growth Expectations

Nvidia was scheduled to release its quarterly financial results after the close of US trading on Tuesday, with investors expected to focus on revenue guidance, customer spending and the company's strategy following the departure of former Chief Executive Jensen Huang.

Interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to face questions about whether Nvidia will maintain its existing approach to providing financial support to customers investing in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Analysts have identified the company's previous forecast for approximately 70% annual revenue growth in its next financial year as a central consideration.

Vital Knowledge analysts said the outlook would have implications beyond Nvidia, given the company's role in supplying processors for AI data centres.

"If management withdraws the 70% target and suggests it is no longer feasible because of leadership changes, export restrictions or adjustments to customer financing, the broader AI sector could face additional selling pressure," the analysts wrote.

Nvidia shares declined in premarket trading after falling more than 4% on Monday.

US Tightens AI Chip Export Controls as Megaspeed Investigation Continues

The US government has introduced additional restrictions intended to prevent Chinese companies from accessing advanced AI computing capabilities through data centres located in third countries.

The measures follow increased scrutiny of international arrangements involving Nvidia processors and cloud computing providers.

The US Commerce Department said on Monday that an investigation into Singapore-based cloud services company Megaspeed began in 2024 over potential violations of semiconductor export regulations.

According to a joint statement from the Commerce Department and Department of Justice, authorities identified possible diversions of advanced semiconductor shipments involving the company.

Bankers are expected to price the Claude chatbot maker's debut on Wednesday and the stock is then projected to begin trading on Thursday, according to media reports.

Despite traditionally being a relative safe haven during times of market ructions, benchmark U.S. Treasury yields have dipped modestly over the last day, as elevated inflation fueled bets on a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December. Speaking on Monday, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh did not provide specific rate guidance, although he flagged that the central bank was attempting to gauge how widespread AI adoption may impact the U.S. economy.

U.S. stock futures are mixed early Tuesday as Wall Street anticipates a historic earnings report from Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA), closely monitors geopolitical shifts involving North Korea, and digests the latest economic data.

The Polymarket traders, a Polygon (CRYPTO: POL) based prediction platform, are leaning slightly bullish for the Nov. 17 trading session. The "S&P 500 (SPX) Up or Down on November 17?" contract currently reflects a 53% chance of a higher open.

Why That Number Matters

Traders are navigating divergent index futures, shifting energy costs, and an extremely high-stakes corporate calendar:

Divergent Index Futures: A nascent tech rebound is contrasting with broader market weakness. Nasdaq 100 futures ticked up 0.23%. However, Dow Jones futures fell 0.31%, Russell 2000 futures dropped 0.37%, and S&P 500 futures slipped 0.05%.

Geopolitics & Oil: Prediction market odds jumped to 18% that President Donald Trump will meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un before year-end, following Trump's comments that a meeting "may" happen at the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China. The geopolitical maneuvering comes as energy markets trend lower; Brent crude slipped 0.78% to $91.72 a barrel, and WTI crude fell 0.94% to $83.68 a barrel.

Nvidia Earnings & Eco Data: All eyes are on Nvidia, which reports third-quarter earnings after the bell in its first major test since CEO Jensen Huang's dramatic resignation last week. The corporate slate also features Home Depot Inc. (NYSE:HD), Walt Disney Co. (NYSE:DIS), and BHP Group Ltd. (NYSE:BHP). On the economic front, October's retail sales and import prices are due at 8:30 a.m. ET, followed by industrial production data at 9:15 a.m. ET.

The Bull Case and Market Outlook

According to Jeffrey Hirsch, Editor-in-Chief of the Stock Trader's Almanac, the market is perfectly positioned for a year-end rally that could run through mid-2027 now that the midterm elections are over. Hirsch argues that the midterms serve as the critical catalyst for the four-year presidential cycle, noting that the "sweet spot" for market returns historically occurs from the fourth quarter of the midterm year through the second quarter of the pre-election year.

Hirsch highlights that the average move from the midterm low to the pre-election year high is roughly 50% for the Dow and 67% for the Nasdaq. He dismisses concerns about the precise makeup of Congress, emphasizing that simply clearing the midterm event risk is what traditionally drives this highly favorable seasonal trend, setting up the market for a sustained rally through mid-2027.
